source.author: verg
source.text: Tum decuit, cum sceptra dabas. En dextra fidesque, quem secum patrios aiunt portare Penates, quem subiisse umeris confectum aetate parentem!
source.text_original: Tum decuit, cum sceptra dabas. — En dextra fidesque, / quem secum patrios aiunt portare Penates, / quem subiisse umeris confectum aetate parentem!
source.text_english: Then it would have been fitting, when you were giving the scepter. See the loyalty of that right hand, he whom they say carries his ancestral Penates with him, he who took his father, worn out by age, upon his shoulders!

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: At ducis imperiis Minyae monituque frequentes puppem umeris subeunt et tento poplite proni decurrunt intrantque fretum.
reuse.text_original: At ducis imperiis Minyae monituque frequentes / puppem umeris subeunt et tento poplite proni / decurrunt intrantque fretum.
reuse.text_english: But at the commander’s orders and under his urging, the many Minyae take up the ship on their shoulders and, with bent knees, run downhill and enter the strait.
